change.author: Joe Au-Yeung

findings.title: Salesforce getClient uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` at line 96 has no `prisma` import. The import block (lines 1-20) has none, and a search of the salesforce folder finds none. Every Salesforce service construction runs `getClient` (constructor, line 57). After the refresh POST it throws a ReferenceError, which also fails type-check. Every Salesforce calendar call then rejects. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

findings.title: Sync gate strips and overwrites stored refresh tokens
findings.body: The branch at line 15 checks only the flags. refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 also requires a user id. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, two cases take `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (lines 5-11): user credentials refreshed through the endpoint, and team/org credentials refreshed directly with the provider. That schema keeps only access_token, because z.object strips the other keys. The placeholder at lines 25-27 then sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers persist the result: zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:104-124 (refresh_token at 120, expiry NaN at 122), office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-270 (spread over the stored key), googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 (key replaced, expiry_date dropped). No error is raised. Fix: apply the minimum schema only to a response that came from the endpoint, and never persist the placeholder.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token is applied in default mode too
findings.body: Lines 25-27 run whatever the flags say. In default mode, office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 spreads the parsed data over the stored credential. refreshTokenResponseSchema makes refresh_token optional (line 56). If Microsoft omits it, the stored refresh_token becomes the literal "refresh_token" and the next refresh fails. Leave the stored value untouched when the response has no refresh_token, instead of writing a placeholder. Confidence is medium because it depends on Microsoft omitting refresh_token; the optional schema suggests the authors expected that.

findings.title: Computed schema keys collapse; expiry check and passthrough are not implemented
findings.body: Lines 8 and 10 use `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as computed keys. Both stringify to the same value, since a zod schema object has no meaningful toString. The second key then replaces the first, so the `z.number()` expiry check the comment at line 7 describes is never applied. Only access_token is required. node_modules is not in the snapshot, so I could not confirm the installed zod version. Intended result: `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()`, plus an explicit expiry check if one is wanted.

findings.title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response that callers read as provider results
findings.body: In sync mode the function returns the endpoint's fetch Response (line 15). Callers read provider-shaped fields from it. googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-95 reads `res?.data`, which is undefined, so the TypeError is swallowed at lines 103-108, which return the stale auth. zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 reads `.data.error` and throws outside any try. zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217 has the same read, caught and logged at 238-240. hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192 reads `.expiresIn` and writes the Response object to the key at 198. The Lark caller (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84) parses the endpoint body as Lark's envelope. Fix: make the sync branch return each provider's shape, or move the switch into each caller.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id as the user id to the sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., credentialId)` at line 93 passes credentialId into the parameter named userId (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3, 11). The endpoint then receives calcomUserId equal to the credential row id, which is a different user in general. Once the response-shape issue is fixed, the returned tokens would be written into this credential at lines 102-109. biginAuth receives the whole credential (line 51), so pass credential.userId through as the other services do.

findings.title: Salesforce connection is built from the pre-refresh token
findings.body: The refresh response is parsed into `accessTokenParsed.data` and saved (lines 90-99). The Connection still uses `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` (lines 105-106), which are the values from before the refresh. The first request therefore goes out with the old token. Use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `.instance_url`. Whether jsforce's own refresh rescues the first call cannot be checked from the repo, because the options passed at lines 101-108 are top-level rather than an oauth2 object.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every service construction
findings.body: The refresh POST and credential write run unconditionally inside getClient, which runs for every constructor call (line 57). Before this PR the stored token was used directly. Refresh only when the stored token is stale, as zohocrm's isTokenValid does.

findings.title: statusText check and dead branch in the Salesforce refresh
findings.body: `response.statusText !== "OK"` (line 86) depends on the reason phrase, not the status. Use `response.ok`, and put Salesforce's error/error_description body into the HttpError message. Lines 92-94 are unreachable: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws instead of returning success:false (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23).

findings.title: Invalid Office 365 refresh responses lose their diagnostics
findings.body: The removed block logged the zod issues and the Microsoft payload. The parse helper now throws a generic Error (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23), and the `tokenResponse.success &&` guard at line 264 is always true. Log the payload before throwing, or restore the previous logging.

findings.title: Sync endpoint contract in the comment does not match the callers
findings.body: Line 7 says the endpoint should return only the access token and expiry date. Callers need more. Teams video (office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:84-95) writes the whole body as the stored key, so a response without refresh_token deletes it. Webex (webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:49-55, 88) requires refresh_token. Google and Lark expect the provider envelope (see the sync-branch finding). An endpoint built from this comment breaks those integrations. Document the exact response shape per provider, or make the callers tolerant of missing fields.

findings.title: Sync request carries no shared secret
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (lines 8-14) sends calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header. The webhook added in this PR requires a shared secret for the reverse direction (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29). If the endpoint returns tokens for any calcomUserId it receives, anyone who can reach it can fetch them. Send a secret header and document it.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with !==
findings.body: The comparison at lines 24-27 is a plain string comparison, not constant time. The repo's cron routes use the same pattern (apps/web/pages/api/cron/syncAppMeta.ts:19), so this matches convention. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers would be stricter.

findings.title: Malformed body and decrypt failures return 500
findings.body: `parse` at line 31 throws ZodError. symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse at lines 57-59 throw on a wrong key length or bad ciphertext. None of these is caught, so the caller gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Use safeParse and return 400, and wrap the decrypt step in try/catch.

findings.title: findFirst then create can duplicate credentials
findings.body: Two concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both see no row (lines 62-92) and both create one. Check whether the Credential table has a unique constraint on (userId, appId). I did not check the Prisma schema.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, and sync depends on the webhook secret
findings.body: `process.env.X && process.env.Y` yields a secret string or undefined, not a boolean (lines 103-104), though the name suggests a boolean. refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 and parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 use this flag as the switch for endpoint sync, so enabling sync also requires the webhook secret and the encryption key. Wrap in `!!(...)` and document the coupling.

findings.title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is out of order in globalEnv
findings.body: Line 207 comes after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (line 206), while the rest of the list is alphabetical. Move it before CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

findings.title: CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no description
findings.body: Unlike the variables around it, this one has no comment. It should say what Cal.com POSTs (form fields calcomUserId and appSlug, no auth header) and what the endpoint must return. Given the response-shape issues in refreshOAuthTokens, the comment is needed.

contracts.action: POST /api/webhook/app-credential writes Credential rows from an external sender
contracts.before_after: createOAuthAppCredential requires req.session and checks team admin rights before creating the row. The webhook checks only the shared header secret and the feature flag, then findFirst plus update or create with decrypted keys for any existing userId, with no session or team scoping.
contracts.visible_effect: The Credential row is created or updated for the target user, and the app shows as installed on that user's next load. There is no UI on this path.
contracts.failure_mode: A malformed body (line 31) or a decrypt or JSON.parse failure (lines 57-59) throws out of the handler, so the caller gets an unhandled 500. Concurrent deliveries can both take the create branch (lines 62-92).

contracts.action: Token refresh delegated to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT for user-owned credentials
contracts.before_after: Before: each caller got its provider library's own result (googleapis res, axios response, provider fetch Response). Sync branch: every caller gets a raw fetch Response from the endpoint, whatever the provider. Callers read .data (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94, zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96, zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217), .expiresIn (hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192), or the Lark envelope (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84).
contracts.visible_effect: Refresh cannot succeed in sync mode for Google, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM or HubSpot. Failures are logged only (zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:238-240, hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:203-205) or swallowed (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:103-108).
contracts.failure_mode: Google: the TypeError at line 95 is caught and the stale auth is returned silently. Zoho Bigin: the TypeError escapes getToken and rejects createEvent. HubSpot: a Response object with an expiryDate computed from undefined is written as the credential key (hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192-198).

contracts.action: Sync-gated token refresh parsing in parseRefreshTokenResponse
contracts.before_after: Before (default mode): the provider schema is validated and its declared fields are kept. With the flags set: minimumTokenResponseSchema keeps only access_token, and a refresh_token placeholder is added (lines 25-27). The gate ignores userId, so team and org credentials refreshed directly with the provider also take this branch.
contracts.visible_effect: Nothing visible. The stored credential loses refresh_token (replaced by the literal "refresh_token") and its expiry fields.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. No error is raised; the next refresh sends the literal string as the refresh token and fails at the provider.

contracts.action: Salesforce token refresh inside getClient, run on every service construction
contracts.before_after: Before this PR the constructor built the jsforce Connection straight from the stored key, with no network call. Now: a POST to login.salesforce.com, a credential write, then a Connection built from the pre-refresh access_token and instance_url (lines 105-106).
contracts.visible_effect: Every Salesforce calendar operation rejects, because prisma is undefined at line 96.
contracts.failure_mode: The ReferenceError at line 96 rejects this.conn (constructor line 57). There is no fallback, and the rejection is unhandled if no method is ever called.

contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-264 (the same function before this PR, using safeParse and logging)
contracts.before_after: Before: an invalid body was logged with the zod issues and the Microsoft payload, and the credential was left unchanged. After: the parse helper throws a generic Error, and on success the spread can overwrite the stored refresh_token with the placeholder (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27).
contracts.visible_effect: getToken rejects, so calendar reads and writes fail for that user.
contracts.failure_mode: Diagnostics are lost. The placeholder refresh_token is persisted when Microsoft omits refresh_token (schema line 56 marks it optional).

contracts.before_after: Before: zoomRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse on the response, then the stored key gets the new access and refresh tokens, plus an expiry from expires_in. After: the parse helper with the sync or team gate keeps only access_token, so refresh_token becomes "refresh_token" and expiry_date becomes NaN (lines 119-122).
contracts.visible_effect: createMeeting catches the failure and throws "Unexpected error" (lines 294-297), so the booker sees a failure.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent corruption of the stored key, as described above; the next refresh fails at Zoom.

contracts.before_after: Before: axios.post called directly, its .data used. After: refreshOAuthTokens with credentialId passed as userId (line 93). In sync mode the call returns a Response, so line 96 throws.
contracts.visible_effect: createEvent and updateEvent reject with a TypeError in sync mode. Default mode is unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: refreshAccessToken has no try block (lines 69-116), so the TypeError escapes getToken. The sync endpoint is also called with the wrong id.

contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204-213 (the axios call this replaced, same function)
contracts.before_after: Default mode: the same axios call. Sync mode: the TypeError at line 217 is caught at lines 238-240.
contracts.visible_effect: Silent to the user. The error is logged, accessToken stays "" (line 71), and the API calls go out with an empty Zoho token and fail.
contracts.failure_mode: Logged only. getToken resolves, so the failure surfaces as API errors later.

contracts.before_after: Default mode: the same createToken call. Sync mode: the endpoint Response gets expiryDate computed from undefined (line 192) and is written as the key (lines 193-200).
contracts.visible_effect: The failure is logged (lines 203-205), and hubspotClient never receives the new access token (line 202 skipped).
contracts.failure_mode: Whether Prisma accepts a fetch Response as Json input at line 198, or throws, is unverified. Either the write fails, or the key is replaced with an object that has no tokens.
contracts.open_question: Does Prisma's Json input at hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:198 serialize a fetch Response to an empty object, or reject it?

contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:85 (the original destructuring of myGoogleAuth.refreshToken, same function)
contracts.before_after: Default mode: the same googleapis refresh, with res.data read at line 94 and parse at line 97. Sync mode: res is a fetch Response, so res.data is undefined and line 95 throws.
contracts.visible_effect: In sync mode the stale token is kept and API calls fail later with auth errors. The error does not reach the user directly.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. Any non-invalid_grant error is swallowed at lines 103-108 and the old auth is returned.

contracts.before_after: Default mode: the same fetch. Sync mode: handleLarkError(resp) parses the endpoint body as the Lark envelope (lines 84-95), reading data.data.* fields.
contracts.visible_effect: In sync mode, a refresh that does not match the Lark envelope throws, and the user sees the error through the failure path.
contracts.failure_mode: Re-thrown at lines 108-111. handleLarkError's behaviour is in packages/app-store/larkcalendar/common.ts, which I did not read.
contracts.open_question: What does handleLarkError do with a non-envelope body?

contracts.before_after: Default mode: the same fetch and the same write-back. Sync mode: the endpoint body is written as the whole key (line 93), so any field the endpoint omits (refresh_token) is dropped.
contracts.visible_effect: Nothing visible while sync is on. Disabling sync later leaves the credential without a refresh_token.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent loss of refresh_token in the stored key when the endpoint returns the shape its comment describes.

contracts.before_after: Default mode: the same fetch. Sync mode: the response is validated with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires refresh_token (line 54), so the response shape the comment describes is rejected.
contracts.visible_effect: In sync mode, meeting creation fails with "Unexpected error" (lines 212-215).
contracts.failure_mode: Reject with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" (line 90). The stored credential is not changed.

contracts.action: Zoho Bigin OAuth start: redirect_uri now a literal
contracts.before_after: The string is the same, because appConfig.slug is "zoho-bigin" (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/config.json:4). Only the source of the value changed.
contracts.failure_mode: None today. If config.json's slug changes, the literal no longer follows it.

summary: Two blockers. (1) packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 uses `prisma` with no import, so every Salesforce calendar call rejects and type-check fails. (2) With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 takes a minimum schema that strips every field except access_token and writes "refresh_token" as a placeholder. Team/org credentials refreshed directly and user credentials refreshed through the endpoint both get this, silently. The PR body's "Refresh oauth token from a specific endpoint" does not work for Google, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM or HubSpot, because refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response that those callers read as provider results. Zoho Bigin also passes the credential id as the user id. The Zoho Bigin redirect_uri change is value-identical. Not verified: the zod .toString() keys (no node_modules in the snapshot), Prisma's handling of a Response as Json, jsforce's own refresh, whether Microsoft omits refresh_token, and Salesforce's response shape. Those are noted as confidence or open questions above. I did not build or run anything.
